notes: Scores how convertible a mechanic is into a Blitz cash tournament. Two kinds of dimension: GATES, where a low score disqualifies the mechanic outright no matter how well it does elsewhere, and WEIGHTED dimensions that trade off against each other. Written as data rather than prose inside a prompt so the criteria can be reviewed, versioned and argued with. Every score must carry a justification and the app_id of a carrier that evidences it.
gating_rule: If any gate dimension scores <= its fail_below value, convertibility_total is set to 0 and the mechanic is reported as REJECTED with the failing gate named. Gates are not averaged in - a mechanic that cannot be run fairly is not partially convertible.

dimensions.label: Symmetric randomness
dimensions.question: Can both players face an identical randomised instance - same seed, same deal, same sequence - so that luck cancels out and the score gap reflects skill alone?
dimensions.note: This is the criterion, not 'is it deterministic'. Solitaire and Bingo contain randomness and still work, because both players get the same shuffle or the same draw. Poker cannot: you cannot deal two opponents the same hand, and the asymmetry is the game.

anchors.1: Outcome is chance with no skill expression at all (slot spin), or players structurally cannot share an instance (hidden private information, asymmetric draws).
anchors.2: Randomness occurs mid-round in response to player action and cannot be replayed identically for an opponent.
anchors.3: Shareable in principle but needs engineering: procedural generation would have to be refactored to accept an external seed.
anchors.4: Randomness is confined to the initial board or deal, which is trivially seedable.
anchors.5: Fully deterministic or already seeded; two players can be handed a provably identical instance.

dimensions.label: Score comparability
dimensions.question: Does a round produce a single numeric score that can be ranked directly against another player's score on the same instance?

anchors.1: No score at all, or progress is a persistent state rather than a round outcome (renovation progress, collection completeness).
anchors.2: Binary win/lose only, with no margin - produces unbreakable ties at scale.
anchors.3: A score exists but is dominated by time spent or purchases rather than play quality.
anchors.4: Clean numeric score; ties possible but resolvable by a secondary criterion such as completion time.
anchors.5: Continuous score with natural tiebreakers, already presented to the player as a round result.

dimensions.label: Round length
dimensions.question: How long does one complete, scoreable round take?
dimensions.note: Blitz's economics need a deposit to convert into several rounds in one sitting. A 40-minute round is not a tournament format.

anchors.1: Hours, or no round boundary at all - play is continuous or session-less.
anchors.3: 5-15 minutes, or variable with a long tail.
anchors.5: Under 2 minutes, tightly bounded by a timer or a fixed board.

dimensions.label: Skill expression
dimensions.question: Within a single round on a fixed instance, does the better player reliably post the better score?
dimensions.note: The highest-weighted dimension. It is what makes the product legally skill gaming rather than gambling, and what makes repeat play rational for a good player.

anchors.2: Skill affects outcome only over many rounds; single-round variance swamps it.
anchors.3: Skill is visible but a weak player wins a single round often.
anchors.4: Clear skill gradient within one round; upsets are uncommon.
anchors.5: Strong, immediately legible skill gradient - speed, accuracy or planning quality dominate the score.

dimensions.label: Learnability
dimensions.question: Can a new player be competent enough to enjoy a paid round after one practice round?

anchors.1: Requires studying systems or meta knowledge before play makes sense.
anchors.4: Rules are obvious from the first screen; mastery is deep but entry is immediate.
anchors.5: Universally known rules needing no explanation at all (solitaire, bingo, pool).

dimensions.label: Asynchronous viability
dimensions.question: Can the match run as two independent rounds scored and compared afterwards, rather than requiring both players live at the same moment?
dimensions.note: Async removes matchmaking latency, lobby abandonment and server cost, and lets a tournament fill over hours instead of seconds.

anchors.1: Requires real-time interaction between players; the opponent's actions change your board.
anchors.2: Real-time by design but a turn-based variant is conceivable with heavy redesign.
anchors.3: Turn-based against a live opponent; playable async with a move-timer and abandonment handling.
anchors.4: Fully solo play; the comparison is purely score-against-score after the fact.
anchors.5: Fully solo, short, and already presented to players as a personal-best score chase.

dimensions.label: Content cost
dimensions.question: How expensive is it to keep supplying fresh, fair instances at tournament volume?

anchors.1: Every instance is hand-authored and consumed once; content is the whole product.
anchors.2: Hand-authored levels with limited procedural reuse.
anchors.3: Mixed: procedural generation exists but needs curation for fairness or difficulty.
anchors.4: Procedural with a solvability or difficulty check.
anchors.5: Infinite and self-balancing from a seed; no authored content needed.

dimensions.label: IP and licence risk
dimensions.question: Can the mechanic be operated without licensed brands, characters or sports rights?

anchors.1: The mechanic is inseparable from a licence - real sports teams, a film franchise, a character roster.
anchors.2: Dominant carriers are licensed; an unlicensed version would lose most of the appeal.
anchors.3: Mixed field; some carriers licensed, some not.
anchors.4: Generic mechanic with incidental theming; one or two carriers hold distinctive trade dress to avoid.
anchors.5: Public-domain or universal rules with no distinctive protected expression.

risk_flags.label: Gambling adjacency
risk_flags.question: Independently of the mechanics, does the mechanic READ as a casino product to a player, a platform reviewer or a regulator?
risk_flags.note: Scored separately from convertibility because it is a presentation and compliance risk rather than a design property. Blitz positions explicitly away from a 'win big' casino pitch, so a mechanic that looks like gambling is a brand problem even when it is provably skill-based. Not legal advice - a flag for a human to check.

anchors.2: Faint association through imagery or terminology only.
anchors.3: Shares surface features with casino products (chips, reels, jackpots) without the structure.
anchors.4: Commonly offered in real-money gambling venues.

excluded_mechanics.skill_cash_arcade: Not a gameplay loop. These are cash-tournament wrappers around other people's mechanics - direct competitors rather than opportunities. Carried as the is_skill_cash flag on their apps instead.
excluded_mechanics.casino_slots: Fails symmetric_seeding and skill_expression outright. Scored and reported as REJECTED rather than omitted, so the rejection is visible.

blitz_portfolio.note: Mechanics Blitz already operates or builds on. Used for the already-yours quadrant and as the known-positive set in the eval harness: these must score in the top decile or the weights are wrong.

output_contract.note: Every dimension must return all three fields. A score without evidence is an opinion with a number attached.

fields.justification: one sentence, under 25 words, stating why this score and not the one above or below
fields.evidence_app_id: app_id of a carrier whose description or reviews support this score, or null with justification starting 'no carrier evidence:'
